context:
Goal: closing a debt proves that its test catches the defect.
Problem (rule): the close check runs the debt's named test file on the commit that made the debt, and needs it to fail. A shared test file (hooks/test_guard.py is named by two debts) can fail there for other reasons. Then the close passes whatever the named test does.
Based on (read): a debt names its test by file path, and the check reads failures per file (lint debt-close code, the lane's read at 15:37 CST).
Based on (ruling): a repo changes to fit a shared tool, never the tool to fit a repo. Asked again because this form is not for one repo. It makes the proof exact in every repo, so the ruling may not cover it.
Departs from: main, which judges a whole test file. Option a adds a path::Class.test_name form.

options.label: Keep file paths only, and file a debt for the weak proof (recommended)
options.lose: A debt that names a shared test file proves less than it seems to.

options.gain: A shared test file proves the right test.
options.label: Add a one-test form, and run only that test on both commits
options.lose: A second form in a shared tool. Goes against your ruling: a repo changes to fit a shared tool, never the tool to fit a repo.

short: Debt close: prove one test, or the whole file
title: May a debt name one test in a shared test file, so its close proves that test?
why: Option a adds a second accepted form to a shared tool, which your ruling keeps for you. The lane works with file paths only until you pick.
